hook: A pair of photographer's flood lamps project the shadow of a young woman reliving, on a six-month loop, the events that end in her death. Content note: the cycle includes explicit sexual encounters and a sustained violent assault, all shown in silhouette, and the file states them plainly. Notice how much of the dread comes from scheduling: maintenance calendars, sealed rooms, thirty-day waits.
whyItMatters:
205 tells a complete story without a single line of dialogue; everything is a shadow pantomime that the observers have to read. Its containment is almost entirely a matter of timing, which makes a burnt-out bulb a real emergency.

The horror seems safely confined to the screen for most of the file, until the incident logs suggest that the distance may not hold.
thingsToNotice:
The cycle plays like a film: a still pose, a photo shoot, months of a model's sociable but lonely life, then in April and October the horned male shadows arrive, meeting her at a party, introducing more of their kind, and being photographed on her old film camera. When she develops the film she reacts with horror, flees home and locks the door, and the horned figures attack her there for the rest of the week; she is strongly implied to be dead well before the assault stops.

On the last day one horned shadow grows as if walking straight at the lamps, which then switch off, and anyone in the dark room suffers what she suffered. The addendum hints at where it all came from, since the second lamp, identical down to its serial number, was found in a ransacked motel room with a similar camera and no trace of the occupant. And when a researcher opened the door mid-cycle, every horned shadow stopped and turned toward him.
